Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the support during our short trial — the team is really encouraged by the latency improvements and hallucination-reduction we saw on the guided triage flow. We finished the 14-day sandbox yesterday and have two asks as we decide next steps:

1) Can you outline options for a short extension vs a timeboxed paid POC (3 months)? Specifically we want a path that lets us: preserve current throughput during evaluation, get some dedicated headroom for peak hours, and avoid a lengthy procurement cycle.

2) What concessions do you offer on pricing for a conversion (trial -> paid POC)? A simple example: convert to an April–June 3-month pilot with a committed baseline and the ability to burst.

We also need SLA guardrails for production-critical endpoints — for example p95 latency and an incident credit model if performance drops during a defined window. Can you share a template or precedent for that?

I've attached a one-page mutual action plan that summarizes Nexos' internal milestones and our procurement timeline. Procurement is looped in on this thread (procurement@nexoshealth.com).

If you can get a quick sketch of options and an estimated cost by EOD Monday, that would help us decide which path to push through procurement.

Best,
Alex

Hi Alex — great to hear the team saw the improvements. Quick reply with three concrete pathways and a couple of clarifying asks so we provide accurate pricing: 

Options we typically recommend (short summary):

- Option A — Timeboxed credit top-up (30–45 days):
  * Add a one-time credit bucket to extend the sandbox. No commitment, same token-based billing. Good if you want more time to validate UX changes.
  * Typical concession: 10% one-time credit on the added bucket for trials converted within 30 days.

- Option B — Short paid POC (3 months) — reserved baseline + burst:
  * Reserved baseline capacity (dedicated) sized to your steady-state QPS plus a burst reserve for spikes.
  * Pricing: committed monthly baseline + pay-as-you-go for burst. We can offer a conversion discount if you commit now (example range 20–30% depending on baseline).

- Option C — Hybrid purchase + success credits:
  * Smaller monthly commitment + milestone-backed usage credits. If you hit agreed UX milestones, some of the committed spend converts into a discount on the first production quarter.

Attachments: I attached a working pricing matrix (Redwood_pilot_pricing_matrix.xlsx) with worked examples for each option and sample numbers for a 100–500 QPS target. Please confirm expected steady-state QPS and expected peak multiplier (x during peak). That will move us from ranges to a line-item quote.

Regarding SLA: we do provide p95 latency SLOs for Dedicated pools with an incident credit policy. Basic outline: 99.9% uptime on the serving control plane, and per-incident credits if p95 exceeds the agreed threshold for a rolling window. For short pilots, we can scope a limited SLA that covers business hours in your primary region (to keep costs aligned).

Proposed next step: 30-min call Wednesday to align on target QPS and success metrics, then David can put a line-item quote in HubSpot and Marissa can draft a minimal MSA addendum for the pilot.

If that works, Alex — what are your success metrics (latency target, freshness/accuracy target, and a deployment milestone we should tie credits to)?

Thanks,
Olga
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Alex / Olga — following up with concrete numbers based on typical Nexos-like patterns. Below are three sketched offers; I can convert any of these to a line-by-line quote once Alex confirms expected steady-state QPS and peak multiplier.

Offer 1 — 45-day credit top-up
- No commitment. Add 500k token credit bucket. Effective discount on added bucket: 10%
- Good for quick validation.

Offer 2 — 3-month paid POC (recommended for prod-like validation)
- Baseline: reserved capacity for 150 QPS steady-state.
- Burst: additional shared burst pool up to 5x for short windows.
- Pricing (example): $26k/month baseline + $0.015 per token for bursts beyond baseline (after bucket).
- Conversion discount: 25% off list if you sign POC within 14 days of quote and commit to minimum $60k total POC spend.

Offer 3 — Hybrid milestone model
- $12k/month commitment + $20k in milestone credits tied to UX/accuracy milestones. If milestones met, credits convert to production discount.

SLA language (pilot addendum):
- For dedicated baseline we can guarantee p95 <= 200ms for inference under the agreed steady-state (with specified sequence length distribution).
- Incident credits: if p95 > 300ms for a rolling 1-hour window during business hours, we issue a service-credit percentage of that month's baseline spend (example: 5–15% depending on severity/duration).
- Canary SLA: we can scope a canary SLA that applies to a limited percentage of requests or a time-of-day window; this reduces exposure while still providing guardrails.

I've uploaded the priced matrix to HubSpot and attached an example quote here. If procurement needs a shorter procurement doc, Marissa can prepare a one-page amendment that references the mutual action plan.

Thanks — this is helpful and much more concrete. Two quick clarifications before we schedule procurement: 

1) Canary SLA: we like the idea of a canary SLA that limits the contractual exposure. Can you provide language that says the SLA applies to a specified subset of endpoints (e.g., 15% of overall traffic) or a time window (8am–8pm ET). We'd prefer the endpoint-based approach.

2) Incident credit threshold: for the pilot we want a simpler threshold: if p95 > 300ms for more than 30 minutes in a rolling window during the pilot, issue a 10% credit of that month's baseline. That gives procurement a clear ask.

If you can insert those two items into the pilot addendum, procurement will review and come back with a PO by EOD Friday. Our primary success metric is p95 <= 250ms for the triage endpoint and a <2% error rate on intent detection after fine-tuning.

I'll share procurement contact details privately to speed review (procurement@nexoshealth.com is CC'd). Happy to do the 30-min call Wednesday if that slot is still open — Alex
